s0.why: 1 describes transitions among sedimentary, metamorphic and igneous rock through geologic time; 5 says processes change one type to another.

s1.why: 2 says each rock type is altered when forced out of equilibrium; 4 names plate tectonics and the water cycle as drivers and says rocks change in new environments.

s2.why: 20 says any pre-existing rock can be modified by metamorphism; 26 says any of the three types can melt and cool into igneous rock.

f0.why: Sentence 1 lists the three main rock types.

f1.why: Sentence 4 names plate tectonics and the water cycle as the driving forces.

f2.why: Sentence 23 says rock cooling within the Earth cools very slowly, giving coarse-grained texture such as granite.

f3.why: Sentence 25 says rapid cooling with no crystals gives a natural glass such as obsidian.

q1.why: 3 says basalt may break down and dissolve when exposed to the atmosphere; 7 and 8 describe weathering fragmenting rock and carrying off dissolved material.

q2.why: 23 ties slow cooling within the Earth to coarse grain; 25 says the rapidly cooled rocks are fine-grained or crystal-free, so the deep one has larger crystals.

q3.why: 10 covers burial and compaction; 11 says a rock of such grains fused together is sedimentary.

q4.why: 26 says any of the three main rock types can melt into magma and cool into igneous rocks.

q5.why: 25 says rocks sometimes cool so rapidly no crystals form, resulting in natural glass such as obsidian.

q6.why: 18 describes an igneous intrusion heating surrounding country rock as a type of metamorphism; 19 names it contact metamorphism driven by the magma's heat.

b0.why: 8 gives breakdown into fragments, 9 transport and deposition, 10 burial and compaction, 12 lithification of these buried fragments; the order is the one the sentences narrate.

b1.why: 23 puts granite, very slow cooling and coarse texture inside the Earth; 24 calls surface-cooled rocks volcanic; 25 places obsidian and basalt among those surface rocks.

b2.why: 3 says basalt may melt as it is subducted under a continent, and 2 gives the reason: rocks alter when forced out of equilibrium.

b3.why: 11 says a grain keeps its original class but a rock of fused grains is sedimentary, so the last step (index 3) is the flawed one.
